units.verdict: Not yet something to be proud of, and not yet at the /th-design bar, though it is now a careful, legible and honest draft rather than a wall. The measured movement is real: the overview went from 30.7 screens to 4.6, words before the thesis from 544 to 141, and stock meta-language from 53/8/23 to 5/0/0, with AA contrast clean in both themes and a static fallback under every diagram. But the reader the owner chose as the bar (requests: title, one-sentence thesis, an eight-line session, routes) would meet 141 words of apparatus before the thesis, no title at all on a phone, sideways scrolling on every page, diagrams cut off at their edges, a glossary with one entry named 'u-term', citations that land at the top of 55-screen files, and no opinion: 0 judgements in 136 claims, with 24 quotes all introduced by 'The project states:'. The deepest problem is not on the page. The site the owner opens is draft rev 5, which the design reviewer had already judged not-ready, and nothing stopped the run from closing on it. Readiness still does not measure what the owner reviews. Fix the gate (D2-M1, D6-M1) and the landing order (D1-M1) first; they are cheap and they change every future dossier.

units.gap: The step commands are well built: a frozen command table (cli.ts:261-435) with JSON/human output that cannot drift (renderHuman), per-session bubblewrap views and a broker socket whose rule admits only that session's commands. The run that is actually used is a different program. All 5 runs on this host were launched with `syzygy polaris`, which is still labelled 'prototype'. polaris.ts drives the step CLI in process: it captures stdout, parses it back as JSON, and reads the result through untyped string keys. It polls the files every 3 s and types messages into the agent TUIs with `tmux send-keys`. The ideal is one typed run engine with an explicit state machine, typed records, an acknowledged message channel to every session, and a close step that seals what actually happened. Today close seals neither the review outcome nor the site of record. In launched mode it also writes fixed sentences that are false.

findings.claim: A launched run's Execution Record makes fixed claims that are false in launched mode. close.ts writes 'Syzygy issued no credential for this run and wrote none to the state directory'. Yet polaris.ts:403-414 copies the operator's ~/.claude/.credentials.json into <stateRoot>/<runId>.agents/<role>/.claude/ for all four roles. Nothing removes the copies at stop or close: 20 copies persist across the 5 runs (paths and modes listed only; contents not read). The 4 older runs' copies are mode 777, and the state root itself is mode 777. Exposure is bounded by ~/.local at 700. NO_PROVIDER_CALL also calls the sessions' provider traffic 'the operator's act', but in launched mode Syzygy started those sessions.

findings.claim: Close seals a run without recording how its reviews ended, and the sealed site misstates the design review. In run-ffe579c7, design verdict 0 (site 0) was validated as not-ready/blocking. Fidelity verdict 6 (draft 6) was also not-ready, and the supervisor stopped blocked with all 6 repair cycles spent. The operator then closed the run by hand. The site of record (site/0, from draft 5) still says in its review-status footer 'Rendered-design review: none counts (no design verdict has been checked) [Unknown]'. record.json has no readiness, final-state or site-of-record field (its 23 keys enumerated), and close.ts reads no review record. Close also builds the record from a different revision than the site. close.ts has no render, site or review stage (CloseStage, close.ts:55). reportedCommands takes latestPassedDraft, which is revision 6 (close.ts:181), while the only site, site/0, renders revision 5. So record.json mixes draft 6's commands with site 0's digests, and nothing says that revision 6 passed check but was never rendered, or why. Correction to the relayed premise: revision 6 did not pass fidelity. fidelity-verdict-6 was validated but declares not-ready (blocking: true), which is why the supervisor did not render it (polaris.ts:712 renders only on a ready fidelity verdict). Leaving site/0 as the site of record is defensible; leaving that choice unstated is the defect.

evidence: run-ffe579c7….supervisor.json: no 'done', stopped 2026-11-08T04:12:06Z; steps.jsonl close at 04:07:27Z

findings.claim: Fidelity repairs, design repairs and drafts that check refuses all draw on one repair budget, and design always comes last. Draft revision n is repair cycle n: check refuses revision > maxRepairCycles (check.ts:172-173), refused drafts included (polaris.ts:60-63). The supervisor stops on a blocking fidelity verdict when draft.n >= max (polaris.ts:547-551). It stops on a blocking design verdict on the same draft count (repairsSpent, polaris.ts:671, 699). The inventory alone has its own count (inventory.ts:155). The design review runs only after fidelity is ready and a site is rendered (polaris.ts:712-723), and each design repair needs a new fidelity round before re-render. In run-ffe579c7 (max 6), the design review got its first and only verdict at draft 5. Revisions 1-4 had gone to check and fidelity repairs, so one design repair was possible. Its fidelity review blocked, and the run ended at the limit. As built, design quality is whatever budget fidelity leaves over.
findings.label: Observed
evidence: run-ffe579c7…/steps.jsonl (check revs 0-6, fidelity verdicts 0-6, design verdict 0)

The run's state is re-derived by a 114-line polling loop that reads files every 3 s. Messages to sessions are typed into their TUIs with `tmux send-keys -l` plus Enter, with no acknowledgement, and that races an agent that is mid-turn.

It can also stop the run as 'inventory repair cycles spent' because of those same rows.

units.gap: As an integrity machine the check is close to world-class. Every citation and quotation is re-derived from Git objects at the pinned revision, Observed is reserved for quotations Syzygy verifies itself, and verdicts are bound to packet digests. What it measures is that a dossier is safe and well formed, not that it is good. About 29 finding kinds are structural. Reader quality reaches the check only as 4 advisory counters, which set no outcome and are not stored. Both readiness gates are LLM sessions, and their verdicts are validated for internal consistency only. The 'rendered-design' reviewer never sees a rendering: it reads 3.4 MB of HTML source. That explains how fidelity and design both reached 'ready' while the owner found 16 problems. The ideal keeps this integrity core. It adds mechanical reader metrics measured on the rendered pages and stored with the run, a design reviewer that looks at pixels, and a typed draft model so the schema is declared once.

findings.claim: The check's outcome measures safety, not quality. By a sweep of `kind: '…'` literals, check-derive.ts emits 27 finding kinds and check.ts 2 more. All 29 are structural: schema, ids, citations resolve, ranges, quotation form and verbatim match, labels, versions, pole validity, question limit. Reader quality is represented only by reader-advice.ts: RS-13 code symbols in titles, RS-14 at most 3 deep dives, RS-16 a diagram per section, RS-19 300 words of prose. These are advice that 'sets no outcome and is not stored in the check record'.
findings.label: Observed

findings.claim: The rendered-design review never sees a rendered page. Its packet is the site's HTML as JSON strings: 3.4 MB in run-ffe579c7. 32% of the site's bytes are inline CSS (1,052,010 of 3,285,836 bytes over 45 pages). Waiting sessions get only Read, Glob, Grep and Bash. No screenshot or browser step exists, although the repo has a CDP harness used for /polaris sweeps and a dossier browser test. Layout, diagram legibility, colour and hue problems are invisible to this reviewer by construction.
findings.label: Observed

findings.claim: A ready verdict means the verdict is self-consistent, not that it is right. validateVerdict checks the schema, packet digest, pinned revision, session identifiers, completeness, quotations and consistency between rows and declared readiness. Blocking is derived from the reviewer's own rows. Nothing independent of the reviewing LLM measures the dossier, which is consistent with REQ-014 ('never a completion oracle'). The evaluation harness that could do so (evaluateDossier, runReaderTest) is wired only to a dev script; see generation-core.
findings.label: Observed

Every consumer walks the draft as `unknown`: 650 bracket string-key reads (x['field']) across dossier product code, including 171 in render.ts, 100 in check-derive.ts and 45 in review-verdict.ts. Three draft schema versions are accepted at once (v2, v3, v4), with field-version and element-version findings. Each schema change has to be re-validated by hand in every reader.

units.gap: The output is sound where it counts. All 1,923 internal links across the 45 pages of the latest site resolve. The SVG is asserted inert. Pages render under a CSP sink contract, and governance identifiers stay off the reading pages. The code that produces it is the weakest part of the codebase to change. Two functions do most of the work. renderDossierSite is one 565-line closure that concatenates HTML strings with 88 manual escape() calls. buildLocalInput is a 473-line adapter that turns the local draft into the parked provider pipeline's draft shape so the old renderer can draw it. The renderer still carries both modes, and the provider mode's output is byte-pinned by a golden file. It lives in the Butlers POC app and overrides that app's theme. Greenfield, it would be a SiteModel built once from a typed draft, with each page type a small pure component, one escaping template, one theme stylesheet and one mode. That would make a new page type or visual element a local change instead of surgery inside a closure.

The file has 86 lines over 200 characters, the longest 731. render.ts's buildLocalInput is a 473-line adapter. Together they are the 2 largest of 400 top-level functions in the Polaris code. units.gap: I traced imports from the dossier package's product files and from the dossier-site renderer's closure. The live path reaches 18 of the core's 27 product modules (3,438 lines): screening and redaction, generation-source, quote locating and verification, closed-schema, canonical JSON, draft-model, local-render types, page-sink and the site evaluation. Those modules are careful, well-bounded code. The other 9 modules (2,097 lines) are the parked provider island: pipeline, discovery, discovery-provider, excerpt, prompts, provider-draft, admitted-input, reader-questions and rendered-design. The live renderer is still shaped by the island's draft model. The package name no longer describes its contents, which are evidence and screening plus site evaluation. The most valuable live-ready asset is unused: a reader-test evaluation harness (evaluateDossier, runReaderTest) that answers frozen reader questions from the rendered site and reports Unknown, never a pass, when evidence is absent. It runs only from a dev script with scripted answers.

That is roughly 1.4-2x the sketch, and the excess is shape, not bulk. A greenfield 'point at a repo URL, get a beautiful dossier' has a few parts. A typed Draft declared once (types, JSON Schema, parser). An Evidence package (pinned Git reads, screening, quotation verification). A RunEngine state machine over typed records, with one acknowledged message channel per session. An Authority snapshot loaded once from the act records and passed in as a port. A SiteModel with page components and one theme. A quality loop: rendered audit, a reader-test session, and stored metrics compared run over run. Against that sketch, the current code is missing the quality loop and the typed model. moves.why: [mandate-grounded] VIS-3 (digestible by a human unfamiliar with the project) is the property no current gate measures; pdja framing finding; TARGETS scoring item 1; L1 ten-second thesis test.
integration_points: status.ts readiness; one-command-run spec (zwja) session list

moves.what: Render regression over every stored draft: a script that re-renders each retained run's checked drafts with the current renderer (no model call, no new read beyond the consented pinned trees) and emits a per-draft scorecard diff: words and bytes per depth, max unbroken prose run, figures per section, label/marker density, broken links, RS advisory counts, page count. Any renderer PR attaches the diff. Drafts are already immutable inputs in run directories.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] VIS-1 reproducibility, rule 6/7 discipline applied to the product; cheapest way to stop renderer regressions reaching the owner's next run.

moves.what: Scored corpus and generator scorecard: a frozen set of pinned targets (one per archetype) with frozen question sets and answer keys; each generator version (brief, schema, standards, renderer digests) is scored on the corpus: comprehension, words-to-all-answers, Unknown share, judgement count, diagram coverage per mechanism, reviewer findings by RS id. Stored as dated evidence records so 'better' is a measured claim across generator changes, not an impression from one Redis run.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] L8, TARGETS 'how a page is scored' and 'unchanged process', REQ-006/014 evaluation; extends N13 (claim ledger + frozen-case corpus) from the parked pipeline to the live one.
integration_points: observation consents per target (pdja.21 launch-time consent)

moves.what: Reference-site comparison: for targets with an official site, the operator captures the reference pages once into the evaluation inputs; a second fresh reader answers the same probes from the reference; the scorecard reports generated-vs-reference comprehension and reader cost. Never an input to authoring, so it cannot leak into the dossier as an unverified external claim.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded for evaluation] TARGETS 'a reference answer exists', L1-L4 came from those sites; keeps REQ-039's line between clone evidence and external text.
integration_points: owner ruling: reference capture is the operator's own act, outside the consent records

moves.what: Declare reader-cost budgets per archetype (first screen <= ~150 words, section <= 300 words, landing <= N bytes) so the size report and design review start from counted pass/fail instead of 'Unknown, no budget declared'.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] RS-7/RS-19, L4, gap-analysis item 19 (owner sign-off on budgets after first measurement — the measurements now exist).

units.gap: [Observed] The site is a well-behaved static document: landing, Pole pages, a deep dive, contents, glossary, sources, review report; reading and evidence views; collapsible navigation and glossary popups landed in pdja.1. As a product it still assumes one reader on one path. The operator is required to name an audience at launch, and it is recorded, but it never reaches the author's brief; the brief and the reader standards instead fix 'an engineer new to the project'. The landing page offers no routing by intent (use it, run it in production, contribute, evaluate it), so every reader takes the same path. Across all 45 rendered pages there is no search and no script (the pdja.5 script-with-static-fallback model is available but unused by the latest render), no skim mode even though the abstraction-tree standard makes headings-plus-opening-sentences a true summary by construction, and no share affordances (per-claim permalinks, preview cards, print/one-file export). The ideal: the landing asks 'what are you here to do?' and routes; the configured audience shapes depth; a skim view turns RS-4 into a feature; search and deep links make the dossier a reference people return to and share; all of it a presentation layer over identical content (VIS-1: simplify presentation, never content).

findings.claim: The audience the launcher requires is dropped before the author sees it: `polaris` refuses to start without one and the run record stores it ('Operators and integrators deploying or building on Redis'), but brief.ts never interpolates it, and the brief's rule 7 refers to 'the stated audience' that the brief never states; RS-2 meanwhile fixes the reader as a newcomer engineer.
findings.label: Observed

findings.claim: No rendered page carries search or any script: 45 HTML files, 0 <script> elements, 0 search inputs.
findings.label: Observed

moves.what: Audience to brief, then persona lenses. Step 1 (bug-sized): put the declared audience in the brief's 'What the dossier answers' and in RS-2's reader sentence. Step 2: optional `personas` (newcomer, operator, contributor, evaluator) where blocks and elements may carry an `audience` tag; the renderer offers a persona switch that changes default expansion and the primary route, never which facts exist (static fallback: everything expanded).
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] VIS-3, VIS-1 (simplify presentation, never content); the launcher already asks the question (polaris.ts:168) so the owner expects it to matter.

moves.what: Reader-intent routes on the landing page: the author writes 3-5 `routes` ('I want to use it', 'I run it in production', 'I want to change it', 'Is it right for me?'), each an ordered list of section/element anchors with a one-line promise; check resolves every anchor; the landing renders them as route cards under the thesis and each page shows 'next on your route'.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] L3 (great sites route by reader intent in the reader's words), RS-24 (always oriented), owner pdja 'navigable pages'.
integration_points: dossier-site.ts landing route cards + per-page next-on-route link

moves.what: Skim view: a reading-view toggle that renders only headings, opening sentences, diagrams and callouts (the RS-4 abstraction-tree summary), so a reader can take the whole dossier in two minutes and drill where they care. Doubles as an evaluation input: the skim text alone is what the comprehension probe's ten-second/two-minute questions are asked against.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] RS-3/RS-4 make this summary true by construction; L4 (short at the top, deep below).

moves.what: Static search and identifier index: build-time inverted index over headings, glossary terms, identifiers and claim text, served as JSON with a small hash-allowed script; the contents page is the no-script fallback. Includes 'where does X live' for every backticked identifier, linking claim -> source page.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] RS-24 orientation; VIS-7 (every link resolves) extends naturally to an index the renderer generates and checks.

moves.what: Shareability: stable per-claim permalinks ('copy link to this claim' with its label and citation), Open Graph preview cards from thesis and title, a print stylesheet and a one-file export (inlined site) for sending a dossier to someone without hosting.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] owner goal of a manifesto people read; VIS-7 stable links.

units.gap: [Observed] A run is one author session reading a one-commit clone from scratch: for Redis 8.10.2 it inspected 22 paths and cited 19 files, and the whole run took about 81 minutes (brief 02:46, close 04:07). That works for a project whose story lives in README, MANIFESTO and a few core C files; it will not scale to a Sentry-sized monorepo, where nothing obliges the author to name every subsystem or to say which it deferred. Cost is invisible: usage is an operator declaration and the latest run recorded none. Every run starts cold: the brief carries no prior run, nothing re-locates the previous dossier's citations at a new revision, and there is no way to show what changed between two revisions, which is exactly what TARGETS' licence-trio portability proof (7.2.4 -> 7.4.0 -> 8.0.0) needs. The ideal: hierarchical exploration with a coverage map Syzygy can check; regeneration that carries forward what still holds and re-verifies what moved; a claim-level dossier diff between revisions; a content-addressed understanding cache keyed by blob id; and measured cost per run so budgets can be set from data.

findings.claim: No regeneration path exists: the brief, check, inventory and step-guard modules carry no prior-run input (0 matches for regenerat|previous run|prior run|incremental across brief.ts, check.ts, inventory.ts, reverify.ts), so a new revision is a full cold run.
findings.label: Observed

findings.claim: Run cost is unrecorded: agentUsage state 'not-recorded' (operator declared none); only the step log's wall clock is known (~81 min).
findings.label: Observed

moves.what: Hierarchical exploration with a checkable coverage map: Syzygy partitions the pinned tree from its path-only census and manifests (workspaces, packages, top-level dirs above a size threshold) into subsystems and puts the partition in the brief; the author dispatches scout subagents per subsystem (same rules, same clone, no execution) that each return a cited subsystem card (purpose, entry points, talks-to); check requires a card or a `deferred-by-budget` entry for every partition member. The cards render as a subsystem atlas (Sentry's 'one line per subsystem' shape) and feed the boundary diagram.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] REQ-polaris-generation-030 (hierarchical, budgeted discovery with deferred-by-budget accounting), L3/L4, VIS-2 (an unvisited subsystem is Unknown, not absent).

moves.what: Carry-forward regeneration: `syzygy dossier init --from <sealed run>` pins a new consented revision, computes the tree diff, re-locates every prior citation at the new revision (same bytes found elsewhere -> moved; changed -> stale; gone -> broken), and issues a brief listing stale and broken blocks plus changed paths; the author repairs only those and re-examines the thesis. Fidelity review covers the changed blocks plus a sample of carried ones.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] VIS-1 reproducibility and VIS-2 currency (stale evidence is not success); TARGETS changed-source regeneration; cuts cost per rerun.

moves.what: Dossier diff page: given two sealed runs of one repository, render 'what changed between A and B': claims retracted, qualified, added, thesis and pillar changes, decision records whose cost changed; keyed by stable block ids and citation re-location, with an Unknown bucket for blocks that cannot be matched. The licence trio is the acceptance test (every licence statement must change).
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] TARGETS portability proof ('retract a claim, qualify a promise'), VIS-2.
integration_points: machine.json claim ids as the join key

moves.what: Content-addressed understanding cache: per-blob and per-subsystem cards keyed by blob id + brief/standards digest + model, reused by later runs when the blob is unchanged; each reuse is disclosed as such, labelled Inferred, never Observed.
moves.why: [vision-extending on retention] keeps cost proportional to change; but storing derived understanding of observed code across runs is a retention posture change, an escalation trigger needing an owner act.

moves.what: Measured cost: when Syzygy launches the sessions (one-command run), capture each session's usage from the agent CLI's structured output into the run record mechanically, with tokens, turns and wall time per stage; publish cost per archetype and repository size so budgets and deadlines are set from data.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] VIS-2 (usage today is Unknown by declaration); gap-analysis item 21 (rate limits / feasibility).
integration_points: run-record.ts agentUsage (observed from subprocess output vs declared)

units.gap: [Observed] Humans steer a run at three points today: the launch configuration, up to N in-session clarification questions, and the owner reading the finished site and filing beads against the generator. In the latest Redis run the author asked 0 of its 3 permitted questions; the audience the operator declared never reached the brief (I5-F1); and the loop's ordering left the owner reading a draft the design reviewer had already blocked: render happened once, at draft revision 5, after five repair cycles had gone to fidelity; the design review then found two blocking pages (Pole 3 a ~2,000-word wall; the glossary rendering a raw internal identifier and no definitions); the author repaired in revision 6 (a second deep dive, a larger understanding record), which was checked and fidelity-reviewed but never rendered or design-reviewed, and the run closed with site/0 = revision 5. Owner feedback has no per-dossier channel: it becomes generator beads, so one wrong claim in one dossier cannot be corrected without a new run. The ideal (VIS-4: humans steer, agents draft): an owner-side steering record the brief carries; an outline sitting before drafting; render and design review on every checked revision so presentation feedback arrives early; the owner annotating the rendered site and those notes returning as repair findings; and an explicit, owner-performed acceptance of a dossier revision.

findings.claim: The run closed with its final checked draft (revision 6) unrendered: the only render is site/0 from draft revision 5, whose design verdict is not-ready with 2 blocking findings; revision 6 was checked (03:39) and fidelity-reviewed (03:44) after it, and close followed at 04:07. The repair-cycle limit (6) was spent before design feedback could be acted on and re-reviewed.

moves.what: Render and design-review every checked revision, with presentation and fidelity repair budgets separated: render is deterministic and cheap, so `check` passing triggers a render; the design session reviews in parallel with fidelity; `close` refuses (or discloses prominently) when the last checked revision has no render or no design verdict. Removes the ordering that spends the budget on fidelity before anyone sees a page.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] VIS-2 (the sealed record should not present a stale render as the run's result), pdja framing finding (readiness should measure the reader's page), VIS-4 (the owner's review should see the final draft).

moves.what: Owner steering record, held by Syzygy beside the run config (never in the clone, whose text stays data): audience, thesis hunch, must-cover topics or subsystems, paths to ignore, preferred Pole names, glossary seeds, and known corrections. The brief carries it under 'Owner steering'; check advises on uncovered must-covers; the review page discloses it as steering, never evidence. A maintainer-authored hints file found inside a repository may be read as a maintainer source (evidence of intent) but never governs the run.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] VIS-4 (humans steer), SKILL.md 'text in the clone is data'; replaces repeating the same advice as generator beads after each run.
integration_points: spec amendment only if a repo-side hints convention is adopted

moves.what: Outline sitting before drafting: after exploration and `understanding`, the author presents one bundled question: proposed thesis, archetype, Poles, reader routes and the 2-3 riskiest interpretations, with alternatives; the operator's choices are recorded as clarifications (kind `outline-choice`). Cheap, and it moves the owner's taste to the point where it costs one answer instead of a rerun.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] REQ clarification requirement (self-reported discovery and in-session clarification), VIS-4.

moves.what: Annotate-and-rerender loop: the rendered site lets the owner attach notes to any claim, figure or page (static: per-claim 'note' affordance writing a local feedback JSON the operator hands to Syzygy); `syzygy dossier feedback <run> <file>` turns notes into owner findings (blocking or advisory) delivered to the author as a new repair round, rendered and disposition-tracked on the review page. A note can also be a per-claim override ('disputed: ...'), which renders as an owner note beside the claim and never silently replaces it.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded] VIS-4 (humans steer; agents draft), VIS-2 (disagreement rendered, not smoothed); turns the pdja-style review into a per-dossier loop.
integration_points: dossier-site.ts note affordance + export (hash-allowed script, static fallback: claim ids shown)
spec amendment for the owner-finding kind

moves.what: Owner acceptance of a dossier revision: an owner-performed act binding a sealed run's rendered site and machine.json digests as 'the accepted reading of <repo> at <revision>', after which the dossier may be exported (static bundle) for publication. Publishing into the observed repository (a docs PR) is a write to someone else's project and needs its own consent class.
moves.why: [vision-extending for publication] VIS-4 (only the owner adopts); a write to an observed repository stretches the read-only observation boundary and needs doctrine/consent growth; acceptance alone is mandate-grounded.
integration_points: new recorder script per AGENTS.md governance-recorder pattern
SEC-2 consent class for repo writes (if publishing)

units.gap: [Inferred] Polaris already has the hard, rare part, a truth discipline (pinned revision, verified quotations, cited claims, Unknown over invention, independent fidelity and design review, a sealed record). What it lacks for 'beautiful and intuitive for any codebase' falls into four groups: (1) a loop that lets the owner see what the reviewers saw: the latest run sealed a stale, design-blocked render; (2) an explicit reader and an explicit argument (audience dropped, no thesis or spine, zero judgements); (3) generality machinery (archetype detection, hierarchical coverage, a diverse corpus); (4) measurement (a comprehension probe and a regression scorecard) so improvements are proven rather than reviewed one Redis run at a time. Visual grammar, decision records, steering and regeneration build on those. Ranked by owner value over build cost, with prerequisites named; none of the list needs a doctrine amendment except publication into an observed repo (I7-M5) and rendering parser-derived structure as Observed (I3-M2), both left off the top 11.

moves.what: [I7-M1] Close the feedback loop on the page itself: render and design-review every checked revision, separate the presentation repair budget from the fidelity one, and refuse or loudly disclose a close whose last checked revision has no render.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; VIS-2, VIS-4] [Observed] The latest Redis run closed with its owner-facing site built from draft revision 5, which the design reviewer had blocked on two pages, while the repaired revision 6 was checked and fidelity-reviewed but never rendered. Every other feature on this list is judged by the owner looking at the rendered site, so a loop that can seal a stale render undermines all of them. It is small: render is deterministic and cheap, and the ordering change is in check/render/close and the skill's step list. Needs a spec touch because the one-command-run and local-agent-mode specs fix the step order.

moves.what: [I5-M1 + I5-M2] Make the reader explicit: wire the declared audience into the brief (bug-sized), then add reader-intent routes on the landing page and optional persona lenses over identical content.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; VIS-3, VIS-1 'simplify presentation, never content', L3] [Observed] The launcher refuses to start without an audience and records it, yet the author never sees it, and the brief's own rule refers to 'the stated audience' it never states. A dossier for 'operators and integrators' and one for 'a newcomer engineer' should choose different depths and routes; today neither the author nor the site knows which it is. Routes ('use it / run it / change it / evaluate it') are the reference sites' strongest pattern and cost a schema field, an anchor check and a landing component.

moves.what: [I2-M1 + I2-M5] Thesis-and-spine: a one-sentence thesis and 3-5 pillars (each with its cost) that every section must serve, rendered as the landing's first screen; and a brief that stops pasting pipeline rules it then overrides.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; REQ-002, L1, L7, pdja outcome] [Observed] Zero judgement marks in seven Redis revisions and no thesis field in the schema: the dossier is organised by four fixed topics, not by an argument. A spine Syzygy can check (pillar -> section resolution) is what turns 'a well-cited catalogue' into 'an opinionated account of why it exists', and it gives the comprehension probe its first question. The brief cleanup removes the self-contradicting 'begin with Inferred:' and 'advantages only as quotations' rules that train the hedged voice the owner rejected.

moves.what: [I4-M1] Comprehension probe as a readiness input: a fresh reader session with only the rendered site answers frozen questions; answers graded against the understanding record and answer keys; result on the review page and in readiness.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; VIS-3, TARGETS scoring, pdja framing finding] Readiness today cannot fail a dossier that is faithful and tidy but incomprehensible; the pdja epic exists because 62/62 'acceptable' pages missed every owner point. The engine (runReaderTest, topic coverage, reader cost) already exists in generation-core and only needs a session kind, a site-only packet and a verdict schema. It is the single feature that makes 'beautiful and intuitive' a measured property instead of the owner's next review.

moves.what: [I4-M2 + I4-M3] Regression and scorecard: re-render every stored draft with each renderer change (free, no model call) and diff layout proxies; then a frozen archetype-diverse corpus with answer keys scored per generator version.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; VIS-1 reproducibility, L8, TARGETS 'unchanged process', extends N13] [Observed] Every generator change is currently validated by the owner's next Redis run. Re-rendering retained drafts is a deterministic regression test available today (cost 2); the corpus scorecard is the larger half that proves generality across archetypes and needs one consent per target (cheaper once pdja.21 launch-time consent lands).

moves.what: [I1-M1 + I1-M2] Archetype awareness: Syzygy fingerprints the repository's shape from the tree listing; the author confirms an archetype; the archetype selects question packs, preferred elements, technology-table dimensions and page templates beneath the four owner topics.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded for fingerprint and packs; spec amendment where the topic set changes] The four topics and the server-shaped technology table were tuned on Redis. A library, a CLI, a monorepo, a framework, an ML project and an IaC repo are each understood through a different first artifact (API, command tree, subsystem atlas, lifecycle, data flow, resource topology). Without archetype detection 'any generalized codebase' depends on one author session rediscovering the right shape every time with no check that it did.

moves.what: [I3-M3 + I3-M1] Show, then tell: a hero artifact after the thesis plus annotated code walks (Syzygy renders the cited lines, the author writes cited margin notes); and a diagram grammar whose kinds match mechanism questions (sequence, layers/containment, state machine, data layout, timeline), each with its own layout.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; L2, RS-16, pdja point 10] [Observed] 0 code elements in the latest draft, 0 figures on the deep-dive page, and one layered-DAG layout behind all six diagram kinds. The hero is cheap and has the highest per-pixel effect on 'intuitive'; the diagram grammar is the bigger build (per-kind schema and layout) and the main lever on 'beautiful' for mechanism pages.

moves.what: [I2-M2] Decision records: context, choice, alternatives the sources name, what it buys, what it costs, basis, evidence, rendered as cards beside their mechanism and gathered into a 'Choices and costs' index; the sanctioned home for marked judgements.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; REQ-002, RS-10/RS-12, owner direction 16] The owner's 'why' and 'trade-offs' live scattered across sections and a flat technology table today. A decision card is the unit engineers recognise (ADR-shaped), gives judgement a bounded place to live, and pairs with REQ-038's maintainer-stated vs reconstructed basis once that lands.

moves.what: [I6-M1] Hierarchical exploration with a checkable coverage map: Syzygy partitions the tree into subsystems; scout subagents return cited subsystem cards; check requires a card or a deferred-by-budget entry for each; cards render as a subsystem atlas.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; REQ-030, VIS-2] [Observed] The latest run read 22 paths and cited 19 files; fine for Redis, blind for a Sentry-sized monorepo, and nothing records what was never looked at. A partition Syzygy computes and checks makes coverage an observed obligation and unvisited parts honest Unknowns, and the atlas is the page monorepo readers need first.

moves.what: [I7-M2 + I7-M3 + I7-M4] Owner steering, end to end: an owner steering record the brief carries; an outline sitting (thesis, archetype, Poles, routes, riskiest interpretations) before drafting; and site annotations that come back as owner findings in a repair round, with per-claim disputes rendered beside the claim.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; VIS-4] Owner taste currently reaches a dossier only as generator beads after a full run. Steering and the outline sitting move it to the cheapest point (one answer before drafting); annotation turns review into a per-dossier loop. The owner-finding kind needs a spec touch; the steering record and outline sitting do not.

moves.what: [I6-M2 + I6-M3] Regeneration and diff: carry a sealed dossier forward to a new revision by re-locating its citations (moved / stale / broken) and repairing only what changed; render a claim-level diff between two revisions, proven on the Redis licence trio.
moves.why: [mandate-grounded; VIS-1, VIS-2, TARGETS changed-source regeneration] Lower priority only because it pays off after the generator stabilises; it is what makes a dossier a living artifact rather than a snapshot, and it cuts rerun cost roughly to the size of the change.
